summary:
Fire Map Germany is a web app that shows every satellite fire detection over Germany from November 2000 to November 2026 (765,054 detections from NASA FIRMS) on an interactive map, and turns them into a burning-activity calendar.

The challenge asks for MODIS and VIIRS hot spots to be made comparable. VIIRS sees smaller fires than MODIS and reports several times as many, so a record that simply joins both sensors jumps in 2012. We convert the MODIS months into the count VIIRS would have reported, using the years in which both sensors flew, and checked the method by hiding one year at a time. It works well where MODIS sees many fires (Argentina, R² 0.98) and is only a rough estimate for Germany, which the app states openly.

Users can draw an area, pick a period, compare any month with the median of that calendar month, and download the detections as CSV.

This matters because farmers, foresters and local authorities need to know whether a fire season is unusual, not which satellite was counting.
details:
What it does and how it works

Fire Map Germany is a static web app. It loads 765,054 fire detections from NASA FIRMS (November 2000 to November 2026) into the browser and draws them with WebGL on a satellite or street map. Users filter by sensor, source type, confidence, radiative power and time of day, move through time on a timeline, select a German state or draw their own rectangle, and download exactly the detections they see as a CSV file.

The harmonized calendar shows every month since 2000 on one scale. MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) do not count the same fires: over Germany VIIRS reports about 4.3 times as many vegetation fires. We aggregate detections to a 0.25° grid per calendar month and convert MODIS months into VIIRS-equivalent counts. Three methods were compared: one constant factor, one factor per calendar month, and a gradient-boosting model with Poisson loss that uses only MODIS features. Each year from 2012 to 2025 was held out once and predicted without being seen.

Benefits and intended impact

A user can ask “is this month unusual for my area?” and get an answer that does not depend on which satellite was flying. Clicking a month compares it with the median of that calendar month and shows it on the map. The intended users are farmers, foresters, fire services and local authorities who want a long, consistent record for a small area.

Tools

Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyArrow, Matplotlib) for download, cleaning, harmonization and validation. JavaScript, HTML and CSS with MapLibre GL JS and WebGL for the app; no backend. Data: NASA FIRMS archive and API (MODIS Collection 6.1, VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Meteosat), NASA Blue Marble via GIBS, OpenStreetMap, Eurostat GISCO boundaries, GeoNames. Hosting: GitHub Pages. Parts of the code and the analysis were generated with Claude (Anthropic).

What is creative

The app lets users switch between the harmonized and the raw calendar, so the artificial break in 2012 is visible instead of hidden. The data is packed into compact binary files, so three quarters of a million detections run in a browser without a server.

Factors we considered

  • Validation without leakage: whole years were held out, never random rows.
  • Honesty about quality: the model works well where MODIS sees many fires (test region Argentina, R² 0.98, monthly error 1,114 against a typical 16,733). For Germany MODIS sees few vegetation fires; there the simple monthly factor is used, it agrees with VIIRS on “above or below the median” in 77 % of months, and the app says that values before 2012 are rough estimates.
  • Static sources: industry and power plants are most detections in Germany, so vegetation fires are shown by default and the other types can be switched on.
  • Missing observations are not the same as no fire.
  • Recent months have no NASA classification yet; known industrial sites are derived from older data and labelled as derived.
  • Sensor positions are coarse (375 m to 1 km), so a dot marks an area, not a field.
  • No API key is exposed: the site uses pre-built data files.
